staticPages.lead: If you are a recruiter, technical manager, founder, engineer, or someone interested in possible cooperation, you can book a short call and send me a brief email with the meeting context.
staticPages.heroNote: Please send a short email after booking. Calendar bookings without email context and confirmation from my side may be cancelled up to 6 hours before the scheduled time.

sections.heading: Who this page is for
sections.description: This page is for people who want to discuss a role, cooperation model, project, or technical topic.
animatedList: Recruiters who want to discuss a role, contract model, seniority level, availability, or technical fit.
Team leaders, CTOs, and engineering managers looking for experienced people for their teams.
Startup founders or CEOs who need senior technical support for product, backend, architecture, integrations, or delivery.
Small business owners who need custom software, internal tools, automation, or integrations.
People looking for mentoring, technical consultation, or a clear cooperation format.

sections.heading: Best way to contact me
sections.description: Book a meeting and provide the meeting context. You can use the additional notes field while booking, or send more detailed information by email afterwards.
animatedList: Book a meeting using the calendar link.
Use the additional notes field to add who you are, who you represent, and what you want to discuss.
If you forgot to include something or could not provide enough context while booking, please send the missing details by email.
When the context is clear, I can confirm the meeting and keep the scheduled time for a focused conversation.

sections.heading: Meeting confirmation
sections.description: Please add enough context so I can understand and confirm the meeting.
animatedParagraphs: Please include the reason for the call and the expected meeting format in the calendar form when booking.
If you forgot to add details during booking or need to provide more context, please send them by email afterwards.
I reserve the right to cancel a calendar booking up to 6 hours before the scheduled time if there is no meeting context and no confirmation from my side.

I also reserve the right to decline or cancel meeting requests that do not seem aligned with my experience, technical background, seniority level, or cooperation preferences, for example roles based mainly on technologies I have not worked with.

sections.heading: What to include
sections.description: Keep it short and concrete. Add this in the calendar notes field or send it by email if it was missing during booking.
items: who you are and who you represent,
what you would like to discuss,
whether this is about recruitment, cooperation, project work, mentoring, or a technical topic,
what kind of conversation you expect,
the preferred cooperation model, if relevant.

sections.heading: Choose how to continue
sections.description: Choose the simplest path: book a meeting with context, send an email first, or return to the main profile page.

cards.title: Book a meeting
cards.description: Choose a time in the calendar and add a short context in the notes field if possible.

cards.title: Send an email first
cards.description: Use email if you want to share more details, send a role description, or clarify whether a meeting makes sense.

cards.title: Return to main page
cards.description: Go back to the main profile page to review my experience, stack, projects, and professional background.

staticPages.description: Everything you need to know before working with Lukasz Komur, a senior backend engineer and solution architect: engagement models, first steps, communication, security and availability for founders, startups and growing teams.

staticPages.lead: A clear picture of how we can work together – from the first conversation to a production-ready result. Whether you are a founder with an idea, a small company with a system that needs attention, or a team that needs senior backend and architecture support, this page answers the practical questions up front.
staticPages.heroNote: Joining an established company or engineering team? I adopt your existing processes, tools and security policies from day one – the details below matter most for direct cooperation.

sections.heading: Who I work with
sections.description: Direct cooperation with a senior engineer works best when you need ownership and expertise without the overhead of a software house or a full in-house team.
animatedParagraphs: Founders and business owners who need someone to design, build or rescue a product – and who want a direct line to the person actually writing and owning the code.
Small companies and early teams that need senior backend or architecture capacity to move faster, make the right technical decisions early, and avoid costly rework later.
Established companies that need an experienced engineer to strengthen an existing team, take ownership of a system, or lead an integration or platform initiative.

sections.heading: What you can expect
sections.description: The principles I bring to every engagement, regardless of its size.

cards.title: Ownership
cards.description: I take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks – from architecture decisions to production readiness and handover.

cards.title: Clear communication
cards.description: Regular, concise updates. Technical topics translated into business impact, risks and decisions you can act on.

cards.title: Pragmatic engineering
cards.description: Solutions sized to the real problem: maintainable, documented and built to be extended by others – no unnecessary complexity.

cards.title: Transparency
cards.description: Honest estimates, early flagging of risks, and clear trade-offs so you always know where the project stands.

sections.heading: How we get started
sections.description: A simple, low-commitment path from first contact to productive work.
animatedList: Intro call – a short, free conversation about your goals, the current situation and where I can help most.
Scope and approach – I propose an engagement model, first milestones and an estimate so you can make an informed decision.
Agreement and access – we confirm the contract, billing and access setup, including any security requirements on your side.
Kick-off – we align on priorities, communication and success criteria, and I start delivering visible progress early.

sections.heading: Engagement models and formalities
sections.description: Flexible cooperation that fits your company, budget and stage.
animatedList: Long-term full-time or part-time cooperation, fixed-scope projects, and short technical missions such as architecture reviews, audits or project rescue.
B2B cooperation with VAT invoicing for companies in Poland and across the European Union.
Contract-based cooperation for clients outside Europe, including the United States – I have worked with US clients and teams and am familiar with their expectations and communication style.
I can work on client-provided equipment or on my own professionally managed macOS setup, depending on your requirements.

sections.heading: Security and access
sections.description: Your code, data and infrastructure are handled with the same care as my own.
animatedList: A secured remote setup with VPN, multi-factor authentication and a password manager for all professional accounts.
Access limited to what the work requires, following least-privilege principles.
Happy to sign an NDA and to follow your internal security policies, device requirements and access procedures before any work begins.

sections.heading: Communication and collaboration
sections.description: Structured enough to keep everyone aligned – light enough not to slow anyone down.
animatedParagraphs: If you already have tools and processes, I join them – repositories, task boards, chat and planning rituals included.
If you are just getting started, I can help set up a lightweight, professional workflow: a task board, a clear definition of done, and short regular updates.
For non-technical stakeholders, I translate technical work into what matters: progress, risks, costs and the next decisions to make.

sections.heading: Availability and time zones
sections.description: Based in Poland (CET / CEST) and working remotely with clients across Europe and North America.
animatedList: Full overlap with European business hours.
Solid afternoon overlap with the US East Coast – for ongoing US cooperation we agree on a fixed daily overlap window that works for both sides.
Flexible for key moments such as releases, handovers, production incidents and important stakeholder meetings.

sections.heading: Impact and non-profit projects
sections.description: I reserve part of my time for projects that genuinely help animals, the planet or human lives – with pro bono or reduced-rate support.
animatedParagraphs: If your organization rescues animals, protects the environment, supports emergency response or builds technology that saves lives, I would be glad to hear about it – even if the project is not commercial.
I can help with platforms, internal tools, automation, integrations or drone-related software that supports your mission.
Capacity for these projects is limited, so reach out early and tell me about your mission – we will find the best way I can contribute.

sections.heading: Ready to talk?
sections.description: To make our first call as useful as possible, it helps to have a rough idea of:
items: The problem you want to solve or the goal you want to reach.
The kind of support you are looking for – hands-on development, architecture, ownership or advisory.
Your preferred timeline and expected level of involvement.
Any existing tools, team setup or security requirements.
Don't have all the answers yet? That's perfectly fine – shaping them together is part of the first conversation.
